FIX151's defence of it -- that it now carries one measured term and that with nothing invisible it legitimately coincides with the write count -- is TRUE ABOUT THE ARITHMETIC and this lane does not dispute it. It is not a defence of the NAME, and the name is what a reader acts on. This lane counted the actual flattened widget appearance placements in the delivered content streams: 216 '/FlatWidget-<id> Do' placements in every one of the six fixtures, distributed [20,12,8,8,12,21,26,1,40,35,33] across the 11 packet pages -- one for every widget the two pinned sources declare. rows.theAllowanceQuestionFIX151Asked: The 1 pt allowance CAN hide something real, and this lane proved it in the same bytes rather than reasoning about it. CONTROL A: an opaque white strip 492.56 pt long and 1.00 pt tall, laid entirely inside the allowance band just below the C-10-CRIMINAL page 1 text field 'undefined' (x 70.52-563.08, y 421.04-422.04 pt) on a scratch copy of the delivered canonical packet, erased 6,135 px of printed form ink -- a 6.8-inch printed rule line, the line an affiant writes on -- all reading solid white 255. At a 0 pt allowance this lane's guard FAILED and named it as one 6,135 px cluster at x 71.28-562.08 y 421.2-421.92. At the shipped 1 pt allowance it PASSED. The scratch file was deleted. CAPACITY, MEASURED: summed over the 11 packet pages, 99,078 printed-ink pixels per fixture lie in the 1 pt band -- inside a widget rectangle grown by 1 pt but outside the rectangle itself. That is the guard's blind band, and it is not small. Worst single pages are packet 9 (34,343 px), 10 (28,392) and 11 (24,023), all C-10-CRIMINAL, where long text fields sit directly on their own printed rule lines. WHAT IT CANNOT HIDE, ALSO MEASURED. (a) On these bytes it hides nothing at all: across all 66 page pairs, lost ink outside every widget rectangle is 0 at 1 pt AND 0 at 0 pt, identical verdicts, so the allowance is not load-bearing for anything FIX151 shipped. (b) It cannot suppress a FAILURE from the defect class it was written for. An inverted-rectangle misplacement displaces the appearance by exactly the rectangle's own height, and the excused band extends only 1 pt beyond the rectangle, so the whole misplacement is hidden only where the rectangle is 1 pt tall or shorter. This lane measured every one of the 216 widgets in both pinned sources: minimum height 8.244 pt (C-10 Check Box3.0.0), minimum width 7.759 pt (C-10 Check Box6.0), nothing at or under 2 pt in either dimension. At the smallest widget in custody the allowance excuses at most 12.1 percent of such a misplacement and 87.9 percent still fires; for the measured 14.358 pt case it excuses 7.0 percent. (c) It cannot silently erase a whole printed WORD: this lane scanned every word of four or more letters on all 11 source pages against all 216 rectangles and found no word that lies wholly outside every rectangle and wholly inside some rectangle's 1 pt band. CONCLUSION: the allowance is sound for the defect it exists to catch and inert on the bytes shipped, but it is a genuine 99,078 px blind band per packet that will silently pass an erased rule line. FIX151's reason for choosing 1 pt over 0 pt is also real -- this lane reproduced the rounding pixels it names, at insetT and insetR of about -0.12 pt on C-10 page 3. The right resolution is not this lane's to make: it is either to keep 1 pt and publish the band's ink capacity beside the verdict, or to drop to 0 pt and excuse rounding by pixel-count rather than by geometry.
rows.theInRectOcclusionFIX151AskedAbout: Adjudicated on the bytes: CORRECT BEHAVIOUR, not a second defect class -- and milder than 'erasing the printed checkbox squares'. This lane reproduced the 390 px exactly and independently, identically in all six fixtures: 194 px on packet page 9 (C-10 page 1) and 196 px on packet page 11 (C-10 page 3), every one of them reading solid white 255 in the delivered raster, every one inside a rectangle the source itself declares, and 0 px outside any rectangle at a 0 pt allowance. Cluster geometry names what is lost. Every cluster is either a 0.24 pt wide by ~7.7 pt tall vertical sliver sitting at insetR 0.85-0.86 from a checkbox rectangle's right edge, or an 8.64 pt wide by 0.24-0.48 pt tall horizontal sliver at the rectangle's top edge. 0.24 pt is ONE PIXEL at 300 dpi. No cluster has the shape, size or position of a glyph; no caption, no statutory text and no printed word is touched -- confirmed separately by the word-multiset check, which finds zero printed words missing from any delivered page. Rendering the affected rectangles side by side settles the mechanism. C-10 Check Box6.0: the source square's border is a 4-5 px stroke; the delivered page GAINS a full border row at the top and LOSES one border column at the right. C-10 Check Box2.2: same, gains a top row, loses a right column. The flattened control repaints the same square about one 300 dpi pixel up and left of where the form prints it. The box is not erased, not thinned away, not made illegible -- it is re-registered by 0.24 pt, which is 0.0033 inch on paper. Per-rectangle ink accounting: of the nine rectangles that lose anything, two end with MORE delivered ink than source ink and seven with a net deficit of 16-65 px against 498-657 px of printed square, so at worst a border stroke thins from five pixel-rows to four. This is exactly the case FIX151's allowance text describes -- 'a flattened control paints its own appearance over its own printed footprint' -- and it is 60 times smaller than, and categorically unlike, the 14.358 pt CR-65 misplacement, which landed outside every rectangle on running statutory text. Reporting it per page rather than hiding it was right; not repairing it was also right. This lane repairs nothing and recommends no repair here.

obligationFindings.REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING: FAIL, and it is the same defect class FIX151 repaired one line above it, in the same list, in the same commit. The guide's 'Blanks you must fill in' directs, with no condition of any kind: 'Complete \"MUNICIPALITY OF\" on C-10-CRIMINAL page 1'. C-10-CRIMINAL page 1 offers two mutually exclusive caption branches, 'STATE OF ALABAMA' and 'MUNICIPALITY OF ____ v. ____, Defendant'. THREE independent things in this repository say the municipal branch is not this route's. (1) This family's own held record: AL.memo.json track al-felony-dwop rules.filing, read by this lane at hash 7d484d63..., says 'File CR-65 in the criminal division of the circuit court in the county where the charges were filed', and the guide quotes it on its own first page. (2) This family's own delivered packet: it writes C-10-CRIMINAL:Check Box1.0, labelled in its own actual-writes.json 'State of Alabama circuit-court caption branch (selection)', routeDetermined true -- and this lane confirmed in the delivered PIXELS that a check mark is actually drawn inside that box on packet page 9 of canonical.pdf. The packet elects the State branch and the guide directs the participant to complete the municipal one, on the same page of the same form. (3) The sibling family FIX151 repaired in the same lane: al-trafficking-set's production-field-map.json classifies the IDENTICAL field C-10-CRIMINAL:MUNICIPALITY OF as completenessDisposition NOT_APPLICABLE_ON_THIS_ROUTE with routeConditionThatMakesItInapplicable naming the same circuit-court rule. al-felony-dwop-set's field map classifies it REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING with requiredBeforeFiling true and reason 'The platform does not hold this participant or case fact; supply it before filing'. The two families cannot both be right about one field of one form, and a felony is not prosecutable in an Alabama municipal court. The document is a sworn Affidavit of Substantial Hardship, so this is a direction to mis-caption a sworn filing. AGGRAVATING: numbered step 4 still reads 'Fill in every blank listed under \"Blanks you must fill in\" below', unconditionally, and the list heading's exception is written as 'except any line marked with a condition' -- the MUNICIPALITY line is marked with no condition, so nothing anywhere in the guide holds a participant back from writing a municipality into a circuit-court State prosecution. The three obligations FIX151's live row named were addressed; this fourth blank of the same class, one line below the two it fixed, was not.

The sibling family shows the correct treatment: al-trafficking-set ticks C-10 Check Box2.2 and its step 5 tells the participant what has been elected and what to do if they are not claiming hardship.
